title: Desert Survival Hydration Simulator
description: The user manages a desert survival scenario where they must monitor a character's hydration and sun exposure levels. By interacting with a water bottle to drink and sunglasses to equip or remove, the user balances body temperature and hydration over a simulated day cycle, keeping vital stats within safe ranges across multiple timed intervals.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements a desert survival hydration simulator. Load SunglassesKhronos.glb and WaterBottle.glb using GLTFLoader from a CDN. Set up a perspective camera at position (0, 1.5, 4) looking at the origin. Add a directional light simulating the sun that slowly rotates across the sky over a 60-second day cycle, changing color from warm orange to harsh white to orange again. Use a sand-colored plane as the ground and a gradient sky background that shifts with the sun position. Place the water bottle on the ground to the right and the sunglasses floating to the left at eye height. Display an HTML overlay HUD showing: Hydration (starts at 80%, decreases 3% every 5 seconds), Sun Exposure (starts at 0%, increases 5% every 5 seconds when sunglasses are off, 1% when on), and Body Temperature (computed from exposure level). The user must perform these interactions: (1) Click the water bottle to pick it up, it attaches to a raised position near center. (2) Click the raised bottle again to drink, increasing hydration by 15% per sip, max 100%, with a tilt animation. The bottle has only 5 sips total shown as a fill indicator. (3) Click sunglasses to equip them, moving them to a head-mount position with a smooth tween, reducing sun exposure gain rate. (4) Click equipped sunglasses to remove them. (5) A refill station appears as a glowing marker on the ground every 20 seconds at a random position; clicking it resets bottle sips to 5. (6) If hydration drops below 20% or exposure exceeds 90%, flash a red warning border. The simulation ends in failure if hydration hits 0% or exposure hits 100%, showing a game-over overlay. Surviving the full 60-second day cycle shows a success screen with final stats. Validate that hydration stays between 0-100 and exposure between 0-100 at each update step. Use OrbitControls with limited vertical rotation. Add subtle particle dust effects using a BufferGeometry point system drifting across the scene.
